pr_title: Don't suggest change to users that will break dags on 1.10.x
pr_body:
We don't have airflow.operators.python etc in 1.10.x, so suggesting
users change this would break their dags currently.

Closes #12895

issue_context.title: from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator does not work
issue_context.body:
This is not necessarily a bug in core Airflow, but the upgrade-check scripts recommend this as a solution when the old 1.10.x version of importing the python operator is used. 

So, there is a mismatch between the core Airflow code and the recommendations given in the upgrade check.

comments: This is the change that users need to make just before updating to 2.0 -- because this won't work with any 1.10.x versions
Perhaps this needs to be suggested as `try ... except ImportError` approach.
DummyOperator falls in to this same boat.

@ashb @kaxil I'm not sure what the issue is since the tradition `from airflow.operators.python_operator` works in 2.0.

This can be fixed post-upgrade.

@dimberman Well to start with: the upgrade check command suggests making a change that will break in 1.10.14.

Secondly people will forget after upgrading ;)

@ashb sure we can make it a soft warning but after 2.0 they should get deprecation warnings (@ryanahamilton would be great if we could add UI elements that warn people if a DAG uses deprecated features though don't know if it's too close to release at this point)
Kamil has already started working on collecting other classes of DAG warnings for display in the UI -- he's got a WIP PR somewhere.
But anyway -- the issue is the upgrade check is suggesting something that would break users dags on 1.10.14, so that check will need updating.
In my dags I used this form: `from airflow.operators.python_operator import PythonOperator` which worked in both 1.10 + 2.0, so maybe a decent % of airflow users wouldn't be affected by this

> In my dags I used this form: `from airflow.operators.python_operator import PythonOperator` which worked in both 1.10 + 2.0, so maybe a decent % of airflow users wouldn't be affected by this

Yup it will work but will raise a deprecation warning in 2.0

Using old path will raise a warning. I think that current suggestion given by airflow upgrade check should be understood as "if you want to make your DAG fully compatible with Airflow 2.0 and limit number of warnings you get change the import path A to import path B". 

I can be wrong, be the check was to help migrate DAGs not to make them 1.10 and 2.0 compatible. Otherwise we have to redesign the checks. If we think that current behaviour  is unclear then we should improve either messages or docs (or both).

@turbaszek  It seems to me that we should try to ensure compatibility with Airflow 1.10 and Airflow 2.0 to be possible step by step. We've specially released backport packages to make this possible. Now users can test each integration one by one. Core operators are a different case, as they cannot be installed as a pip package. For this reason, it seems that some minor changes may still be needed.

Earlier thread that covered this topic.
https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/11178#issuecomment-731043815

I've been working on displaying the warnings in the IU and it's almost done. I can do it tonight.
https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/11960

Yeah -- with the exception of the core operators all the other changes suggested by upgrade-check will work on 1.10.14 and 2.0.0 -- for instance see https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/12930 where we suggest (1.10.14 -> upgrade check -> fix warnings -> 2.0.0) so we'll need to make it very clear which ones can be done on 1.10.14 and which can't.

> Yeah -- with the exception of the core operators all the other changes suggested by upgrade-check will work on 1.10.14 and 2.0.0 -- for instance see #12930 where we suggest (1.10.14 -> upgrade check -> fix warnings -> 2.0.0) so we'll need to make it very clear which ones can be done on 1.10.14 and which can't.

Or maybe RC5 with those operators added to 1.10.14 ?
I'd rather a 1.10.15 if we wanted to do that -- lets get 1.10.14 out already!
